def: A fetal heart rate tracing suggesting possible fetal hypoxia or acidosis, such as late decelerations or minimal variability. It may prompt intervention or expedited delivery.
Removal of a conjugated group, such as gut bacteria cleaving glucuronic acid from bilirubin glucuronide to allow reabsorption, or cleaving bile salts.
A limp in which the stance phase on the painful limb is shortened to reduce weight-bearing.
The variation in blood flow or pressure between systole and diastole in a vessel. Reduced pulsatility is seen beyond a stenosis.
A VMAT2 inhibitor that depletes monoamine stores. Used for chorea in Huntington disease and tardive dyskinesia.
A falsely low measured sodium when plasma contains excess lipids or protein, which displace water. Plasma osmolality is normal.
Abnormal heart rhythms, also called arrhythmias.
A brand of subdermal progestin (etonogestrel) contraceptive implant, effective for about three years.
Having a single cavity or compartment, as in a simple ovarian cyst.
Relating to endometriosis, endometrial-like tissue growing outside the uterus.
Derived from the same individual, as in autologous blood donation or autologous stem cell transplant.
Thinning and shortening of the cervix during late pregnancy and labor, measured as a percentage.
Prolapse of the urethra into the anterior vaginal wall, from weak pelvic support.
The smooth triangular area of the bladder floor between the two ureteral openings and the internal urethral orifice.
Describing the ability to perceive spatial relationships. Impaired in right parietal lesions and Alzheimer disease.
Describing reduced movement, such as hypokinetic Parkinson disease, or reduced heart wall motion.
Brighter than surrounding tissue on an MRI image.
Mental activity, including thinking, reasoning and awareness. Altered mentation means a change in level of consciousness or cognition.
The salt form of hyaluronic acid, a large glycosaminoglycan found in joint fluid and skin. Injected into osteoarthritic joints.
A pregnancy continuing past 42 weeks. Risks include meconium aspiration, macrosomia and placental insufficiency.
Abnormal fetal growth from placental insufficiency, giving a thin, wasted newborn with peeling, loose skin.
Partial reduction in airflow during sleep, with 30% or greater decrease lasting 10 seconds and desaturation. Counted with apneas in the apnea-hypopnea index.
Surgical opening of a fistula tract, as in anal fistula, to let it heal from the base.
A selective 5-HT2A inverse agonist antipsychotic without dopamine blockade, used for Parkinson disease psychosis.
An alpha-2 agonist eye drop that dilates a Horner syndrome pupil via denervation supersensitivity, used diagnostically.
Surgical fixation of a prolapsed rectum to the sacrum.
A sexual disorder with persistent difficulty with vaginal penetration, pelvic pain or fear of pain.
Relating to cartilage, as in chondral injury of the knee joint surface.
Air-filled bronchi seen against opaque, fluid- or cell-filled alveoli on chest imaging, as in pneumonia.
Resembling lichen planus, with flat-topped, purple, itchy papules or a band-like lymphocyte infiltrate at the dermoepidermal junction.
Relating to scintigraphy, nuclear imaging in which a gamma camera maps radiotracer uptake, as in thyroid or bone scans.
A wavelike, compressible feeling on palpation of a swelling, indicating a pocket of fluid such as an abscess.
Precipitation of proteins when serum is chilled. It occurs in cryoglobulinemia, and cryoprecipitate is a blood product rich in fibrinogen and factor VIII.
A radioactive element (Tc-99m) used in nuclear imaging of bone, thyroid, heart and Meckel diverticulum.
Interruption of blood supply to a tissue or organ, such as surgical or ischemic loss of perfusion.
Interruption of blood supply to a tissue or organ, such as surgical or ischemic loss of perfusion.
Labeling tissue with antibodies attached to a dye or enzyme to show specific proteins. Used to classify tumors.
Relating to the stomach and jejunum, as in a gastrojejunostomy connection or marginal ulcer.
A graph of a person's hearing thresholds at different sound frequencies.
Arising in multiple sites or lymph node regions, as in multicentric Castleman disease.
Confined to a single site or lymph node region, as in unicentric Castleman disease.
Deficient amniotic fluid, with an amniotic fluid index under 5 cm. Causes include renal agenesis and ruptured membranes, and can lead to pulmonary hypoplasia.
An imaging method using rotating X-rays and computer reconstruction to produce cross-sectional images of the body.
The double-stranded molecule that stores genetic information, made of nucleotides with adenine, thymine, guanine and cytosine.
Relating to the digestive tract, from the mouth to the anus.
A retrovirus that infects CD4 T cells and causes AIDS.
The brain and spinal cord.
Oxygen-carrying blood cells (erythrocytes).
A single-stranded nucleic acid with ribose and uracil that carries out protein synthesis (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA) and gene regulation.
Drugs like ibuprofen and naproxen that block cyclooxygenase, reducing prostaglandins and inflammation. Side effects include peptic ulcers and kidney injury.
An imaging method that uses strong magnetic fields and radio waves, with no ionizing radiation, to image soft tissues.
The most abundant antibody in serum and the only one crossing the placenta. It drives the secondary immune response.
A recording of the heart's electrical activity from skin electrodes.
A radiograph of the chest used to image the lungs, heart and mediastinum.
Death of heart muscle from sudden loss of coronary blood flow, usually from a ruptured atherosclerotic plaque with thrombosis.
A pituitary gonadotropin that triggers ovulation and stimulates testosterone production in Leydig cells.
A hormone from the posterior pituitary (vasopressin) that makes the collecting duct reabsorb water by inserting aquaporin-2.
